So, my recipe did not have specific measurements, and it was missing the oils I really wanted.

What I used:

  • Coconut Oil (It's a solid when you buy it but melts at, something like, 76 degrees Fahrenheit which is less than your body temp).

  • Unscented Almond Oil.

  • Vitamin E Oil.

  • A Red Solo Cup shot glass, because I had nothing else to use, and that fucker is awesome! (It's also way too big to accurately measure 1 oz. of oil.)

My Measurements:

Apprx. 5/8 Unscented Almod Oil, 1/8 Vitamin E Oil, and 2/8 Coconut Oil. If I had my say these would have been smaller, and there would have been Sandalwood Oil for the boss scent, and possibly a little Peppermint Oil for that aftershave tightness.

Now, some of you will remember my after work, uncared for or touched, verification squircle, if not, look at that horrible, oddly thick then thin mess. That's what mine looks like without a brush or oil. With a brush it looks a little less scraggly, but still just as messy.

After the DIY Oil Beardly Awesomesauce

Fist off, my experience with beard oils is limited. Most of my facial hair life has been all natural, slanted, scraggly-ass. and hobo-looking growth. Then a tight trim and start over. Why? Because, I was usually poor and lazy as fuck. But, I've played with some cheap beard oil, and using just Coconut Oil (That shit is good for your skin. Seriously, it makes it younger, softer, and if you've had kids and your wife got stretch marks it's an easy cheap way to help with them. Just be smart about how you bring it up. I'm not gonna feel bad if she kills you.)

Ok, moving on, I applied it in a way that pretty closely resembled this, but I fluffed it out with the comb before using the oil. And, I used the same amount. About, five drops. It seemed like a lot as I was doing it, but it worked for my little beard. You may have to dab a little extra oil off your skin when you're done. But, as long as you don't look glittery like a Twilight vampire leave the rest. It's good for your skin, yo. Manly doesn't mean ugh. Even if we tend not to care as much.

Anyways, after using the oil

I took my brush (it's a lot more stiff than I wanted... I bought it from the special hair section of Walmart) and brushed my beard gently. It turned out very soft, and smooth. And had a nice sheen to it. In the light I thought it was more shiny than I was comfortable with, but my wife (and passerby) commented on how nice and clean it looked.

So, if your lazy and didn't want to read all this to see the outcome

Follow the links, read my very basic recipe, and look at these...

Apparently I can't get a picture to upload of the bottle I used for my beard oil. But, the SirPoppycock Coconutty Special Beard Oil comes in one of those plain, brown 1oz. bottles with the dropper. If you don't have one laying around, and Walmart doesn't have them, try looking at a health or New Age store. Both of those love essential oils, and bottles to put them in.

AND

My oiled beardage

Sorry for the shit pictures, I have a severly abused LG G2, and she can't take pictures worth a fuck...

My Overall Rating

10/10

Seriously, my beard is much softer, healthier looking and feeling, smells better, and people notice the sheen but it isn't overbearing. The smell is a slight hint of Coconut (even though I wish it was more Sandalwood or leathery, beacause I love both smells and they seem more manly than coconut), and people noticed, and complimented it. The initial investment seems steep. The Almond Oil at Walmart was right at $5, and the Vitamin E Oil also at Walmart was about $3/$4. and the Coconut Oil at Aldi's (a cheap as fuck grocery store) was only about $2. But, you can make bottle after bottle of 1oz., long lasting oil with these. Well worth the investment, and cheaper than what beard oil usually goes for.

I think everyone should start doing a little DIY Beard Oil personally. It may take a few tries to get your measurements down, and to get the right amount on your beard, but it is well worth the effort. Both in expense, and for the health of your skin and beard.
